correctness.rationale: The claim specifies normalized circle Haar p-moments, all complex coefficient pairs except (0,0), every integer m>=2 and 2<p<4. Chebyshev–Rodrigues integration by parts proves each alias coefficient at k>=2 has sign (-1)^k. Differentiating positive integral kernels and c0 yields the strict all-r derivative lower bound d/dr log(|c_k|/c0)>=k/[r(1+r)]>0 for k>s, proving balanced coefficients uniquely maximize the sum of normalized absolute aliases. Root-of-unity Fourier aliasing then gives the sharp constant; phase equality forces a node zero, and the second alias excludes negative orientation. The beta–Gamma reflection formula proves the exact series; Gamma ratios and a summable majorant justify the large-grid asymptotic. The sin-cubed sum produces the exact cubic cotangent formula, with direct polynomial endpoint resonance. A standalone checker reproduces 3307 finite diagnostics; numeric checks are not used to infer infinite-domain conclusions.

Dai–Kosov arXiv:2611.05930v1 covers iid random sampling for p<=2.
Trefethen–Weideman SIAM Review 2014 develops the trapezoidal Fourier aliasing principle and convergence bounds, but its scope does not determine the present sharp coefficient-optimized equality set.

Marzo–Seip (2009) proves a uniform polynomial Lp norm equivalence for regular and perturbed roots of unity with degree-independent bounds, and a sharp angular perturbation threshold, rather than an exact fixed-degree two-mode constant and all equality cases.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General high-probability iid sample-complexity upper bounds do not imply an exact signed relative error at a prescribed deterministic m-gon, even though their p-range includes the present case. Classical aliasing determines errors for each fixed function but does not optimize their ratio over all coefficients. Neither known result logically dominates the claimed sharp constant and complete extremizers. The original Marzo–Seip 8-page proof was read: its degree-uniform constants and sharp perturbation threshold do not specify the present fixed-degree optimization.

originality.rationale: Closest identical circle object in the public 2026 mathematical record covers only 1<p<2, proving opposite signed sampling distortion. The new p>2 branch needs a different sharp normalized Fourier-coefficient growth inequality. The most directly relevant p>2 primary preprint (Dai–Kosov–Murasko, Nov6 2026) yields iid random sample-complexity bounds and its discrete-coordinate sharpness examples do not entail the exact deterministic m-gon formula, all extremizers, the cubic closed form or quartic two-node transition. Targeted published-finding corpus and external literature queries disclosed no stronger covering theorem; priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A classical periodic quadrature paper or pre-existing 2<p<4 special-case norming theorem could contain an equivalent result under different terminology; absence from the searches does not establish publication priority.
The full Trefethen–Weideman paper was not inspected, so no full-document noncoverage finding is asserted for that source.

value.rationale: For a canonical two-dimensional complex polynomial space the theorem gives the exact worst relative error of every regular m-point sampling operator for an entire superquadratic interval, plus a complete equality classification. The result identifies a sharp change from underestimation in the concave p<2 regime to overestimation, a new finite cotangent formula for the cubic moment, the sharp m^{-(p+1)} rate and the nontrivial m=2 versus m>=3 resonance as p approaches four. The exact signed distortion and equality rigidity have direct quantitative use for deterministic norm discretization and are not fixed-parameter normalization exercises.
